items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well yeah, and Alito, his band broke up, he might just take up another man's band entirely.

ctx.x: Yes, and whether Les Brown had joined this Don Gann band, or whether he just took it over, or whether he may have been an arranger for it. Quite often the kind of story that you heard about how a band originated was romanticized, you know. And it'd give you the impression that this band had stuck together and fought its way up writers and movies and things like to depict things that way. That was hardly ever true. Very seldom did it happen. Usually as the band moved up, the personnel changed. Got better.
Well yeah, and Alito, his band broke up, he might just take up another man's band entirely.
Or higher, and anyway, temperaments being what they were, very few musicians could stand anybody very long in there. Always splitting up, moving up, moving around.
